A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAST-MoE-RL research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and technical appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial layout changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation-based training and evaluation using San Francisco ride-hailing data, including baseline comparisons, ablations, robustness tests, and three-seed results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and the appendices, including Tables 1–7 and the training, expert-activation, and multiplier plots.

M1.justification: The RAST-MDP, travel-time surrogate, adaptive reward, pooled-state MoE encoder, and PPO/GRPO procedures remain unchanged. Section 5.1 adds an explanation of global coordination through pooled states, which were already part of v1's architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2019 CPUC San Francisco data and held-out demand regimes. Global travel-time perturbations and localized incident scenarios already appear in v1 Appendix J and are retained in v2 Appendix I.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same RL algorithms, MoE configurations, dense Transformers, GNN, MLP variants, and heuristic methods. Table 2 preserves both Instant Matching and the 20-second Constant-Interval Batch Matching comparator.

E3.justification: Temporal splitting, evaluation metrics, model configurations, reward-weight sweeps, tolerance settings, and shock protocols are unchanged. Table 4 retains the same training hyperparameters; the expanded discussion of the 5% tolerance does not change its setting.

E4.justification: Architecture and optimizer ablations, expert masking, activation heatmaps, reward-weight and tolerance sensitivity, shock robustness, and multiplier trajectories are all retained. Analyses described as additional or new in the appendices were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three seeds, 42, 456, and 2024, and the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in Table 3. No repeated-run count, uncertainty procedure, or significance test is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains matching/pickup waits of 182/523 seconds for MoE (16,4) with PPO and 192/545 seconds for the 48M PPO Transformer. The delay-reduction percentages added to v2's conclusion already appeared in v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, MFD aggregation derivations, GRPO equations, and conditional multiplier-stability argument are retained. v1 Appendix K becomes v2 Appendix J; the added main-text convergence explanation supplies no new proof or formal result.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions and claims about the 12M-parameter model, performance, robustness, and specialization remain. Although the rewritten abstract omits the explicit 13% reward improvement, v2 retains it elsewhere. The concluding broader-applicability message was already expressed in v1.

C2.justification: The new Impact Statement expands interpretations to deployment safety, edge computing, and potential benefits for underserved areas. It replaces v1's explicit call for future fairness, equity, and labor evaluation with more affirmative benefit statements and a monitoring recommendation. These are interpretive changes without new supporting evaluations.

D1.justification: v2 removes the Reproducibility Statement promising a public repository with preprocessing, simulator, and training/evaluation scripts. No replacement code-access information appears. Technical appendices and hyperparameters remain; the evidence establishes removal of a release disclosure, not withdrawal of an available repository.

R1.justification: Related Work moves unchanged from v1 Appendix A to v2 Section 2. The earlier DRBO conference citation is dropped while the same calibration framework remains cited through its 2025 journal treatment. Research positioning and substantive literature coverage remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, adds brief methodological explanations, moves Related Work into the main text, replaces the Ethics Statement with an Impact Statement, and removes the reproducibility and LLM-use statements. Front matter is updated, but most scientific prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The main paper and references change from a single-column format to two columns, substantially resizing and repositioning figures, tables, and captions. Figures 2–5 become much smaller, while appendix displays are reflowed. All seven figures and seven tables retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The clearer coordination explanation and more prominent related work are useful. However, v2 replaces explicit fairness-evaluation caveats with untested assurances about deployment safety and preventing neglect of individual requests, while removing the planned code-release disclosure. These changes modestly weaken qualification and transparency. The underlying methods, theory, and empirical evidence remain intact, limiting the deterioration.
